chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you buy your sacrificial animal, face it towards the Qiblah, slaughter it or cut its throat, and say: "I turned my face towards the One who created the heavens and the earth, Hanif, and I am not of the polytheists... Indeed my prayer, my sacrifice, my living, and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, no partner has He, and I am commanded [by Him], and I am of the Muslims. O Allah, from You and to You, in the name of Allah and by Allah, Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, accept from me." Then move the knife and do not let it fall until it dies.' And if a person forgets to mention Allah's name over his sacrificial animal, there is no harm in it, and he should mention it when eating it. Narrated.
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended steps and supplications for slaughtering an animal for sacrifice in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the ritual slaughter (*dhabh*) of the sacrificial animal (*hady*), emphasizing the orientation towards the Qiblah and the recitation of Surah Al-An'am verses to affirm monotheism (*tawhid*) and the Prophet's command. It further specifies practical etiquette, such as keeping the knife sharp to minimize pain and the validity of the sacrifice if the name of Allah is forgotten, with the supplicant merely naming Allah at the time of consumption. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on combining precise ritual actions with spiritual intentionality during acts of worship.
